analysis.title: Global Precious Metals Comment: Gold: expectations vs reality
key_insights: UBS stays positive on gold but cuts its end-2026 target to $4,500 after Q3 weakness. The end-2027 forecast is unchanged at $5,000. UBS particularly favours being long gold against the euro.
Gold is at its lowest level since late 2025 and down more than 30% from the all-time high set at the start of 2026.
UBS names three headwinds: the shift in Fed policy expectations with higher yields and an ongoing hiking cycle, a stronger dollar, and competition for investor attention from AI, tech and energy.

The latest leg lower is attributed to positioning, not a change in regime. Gold followed the cut in gross US equity exposure, especially tech, and likely served as a source of liquidity after the US mid-term elections and another reassessment of Fed expectations.

Net speculative gold positions rose by more than 1 moz as of 10 November. A strong CPI print and hawkish Fed commentary then pushed yields and the DXY up, and UBS sees an unwind of those added positions as the likely driver of the latest weakness.
UBS expects traders to be more cautious about adding shorts at these depressed levels. Gold risk-reversal skew now favours puts over calls.

Long-term investors are hesitant but not capitulating. Gold ETF holdings have been resilient and UBS expects OTC holdings to be similarly durable. Another significant price decline would test investors' conviction and pain thresholds.

Central bank buying has been a steady support. Official-sector purchases in the first three quarters exceeded the same period last year, contrary to UBS's start-of-year expectation, and buying accelerated as prices fell. UBS expects this to continue through the rest of 2026.
Physical gold flows into China have surprised to the upside in 2026 and UBS expects them to help cushion pullbacks.

UBS expects support around $3,800 to hold. A convincing break below could shift focus to $3,500. Triggers could be a growth reacceleration that prompts more Fed tightening, or a liquidity event that causes a broad cross-asset sell-off.
UBS suggests it may be prudent to wait with the December FOMC in focus. Market discussion of a potential 50bp hike suggests the bar for further hawkish repricing is high.

The long-term case rests on debt and fiscal concerns and unease that something could break, whether AI disappointment, a bond yield overshoot or monetary policy missteps. Confidence in baseline scenarios is at historical lows.

tension_points.bull_case: The sell-off is positioning-led rather than a regime change. ETF holdings are resilient, central banks are buying more than last year, China physical flows are strong, and traders may be cautious about adding shorts at depressed levels.
tension_points.bear_case: Real rates are high, the Fed is still hiking, the dollar is strong, and AI and energy are drawing investor attention. Gold is near its lows and further declines would test investor conviction.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A convincing break below $3,800 support, which could shift focus to $3,500.

theme_stances.key_argument: The recent sell-off is more about positioning than a change in regime, although a recovery may require patience.
